messages.subject: using own function in ddply
parts:
Hi,

I have the follwing df and code:

df <- data.frame(t = c(1,1,2,2,2), a = c(8,4,9,3,4), b = c(10,3,4,NA,
5), c=c(1,2,3,4,5))
df
diff <- function(df, v1, v2){
df <- df[,c(v1,v2)]
diff <- mean(df[,v1]-df[,v2], na.rm=T)
diff
}
dlply(df, .(t), transform, ab.diff = diff(x, 'a', 'b'), ac.diff = diff
(x, 'b', 'c'))

As you might imagine, that's just an example of an own function, which
does something to two or more variables within a data.frame.
Furthermore, I want to be in control of the variable names when I call
the function within ddply/dlply. diff() is much too complex for its
purpose in this example, but my original function is much more complex
and relies on the new df within the function.
Can you point me into the correct direction?

Thanks, Stefan

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: using own function in ddply
parts:
Hi Stefan,

I'd write your function like this

my_diff <- function(a, b) mean(a - b, na.rm = T)

and then call it like:

dlply(df, .(t), transform,
ab.diff = my_diff(a, b),
ac.diff = my_diff(b, c))

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: using own function in ddply
parts:
> Another problem I can not solve myself: Is it possible to combine
> computations within the splitted parts of a df with ones over the whole
> dataframe?
>
> Scenario: I want to relate the mean differences from my example below to
> the mean difference, of say a and b, regarding the whole dataframe.
>
> Before I start to build a function which does this job by computing the
> mean difference for the whole df first and than starting dlply with the
> mean as argument, is there another, more convenient way to do this?
It doesn't seem like you much of need a function for this
my_diff <- function(a, b) mean(a - b, na.rm = T)

df <- transform(df, ab.diff.overall = my_diff(a, b))
dlply(df, .(t), transform, ab.diff.group = my_diff(a, b))

Hadley
